m:nevsky: The cathedral is open every day from 7am to 7pm and entry is free (Google listing and recent guides); it's a working church, so during services visit quietly with shoulders and knees covered. The Crypt of icons (museum) is open Tuesday to Sunday 10am–6pm, last entry 5:30pm, closed on Mondays and public holidays: ticket €10 (National Gallery website; on Thursdays it costs €2). Cathedral price and hours to be confirmed.
m:serdica: The Serdica archaeological complex is open Tuesday to Sunday 10am–6pm and closed on Mondays, free entry (Google listing, to be confirmed); the ruins in the metro passages can always be seen. The Rotunda of St George, from the 4th century and with medieval frescoes, is open every day 8am–7:30pm (working church, free entry). Sveta Nedelya Cathedral is open 7am–7pm (free entry).
m:banya: The mosque is an active place of worship: the Google listing says it's open 10:30am–10pm, but you can only go in outside prayer times, with shoulders and legs covered and shoes off. The Central Synagogue is open Monday–Friday and Sunday 9am–5pm, closed on Saturdays; according to a recent review the ticket costs €10, you need ID and there's a security check (to be confirmed). The Central Market is open every day 7am–10pm.
m:vitosha: The street and the garden are free to walk at any hour. The theatre can be seen from outside; to go in you need a performance ticket (programme on the theatre's website). On the main street café prices are higher: to eat better, move into the side streets.
m:archeo: Open every day 10am–6pm, last entry 30 minutes before closing (Google listing and recent guides for summer hours, winter to be confirmed on naim.bg). Ticket about €6 (2026 reviews and guides, price list not seen); free on the last Sunday of the month (to be confirmed).
m:sofiachurch: The basilica is open every day 7am–6pm; access to the underground museum starts around 10am and has a small ticket (a few euros, amount to be confirmed). The Russian Church is open every day 8am–6:30pm and is free (Google listing).
m:boyana: Open every day: from April to October 9:30am–6pm (ticket office until 5:30pm), from November to March 9am–5:30pm (ticket office until 5pm), from the church's website. Ticket about €6 (2026 guides and reviews, price list not read on the website). Only 9–10 people go in at a time, for about 10 minutes, and no photos: at peak times you can wait up to an hour. Booking by phone (+359 2 959 09 39) or email on weekdays is recommended. It's about 8 km from the centre: taxi about 20 minutes, or bus 64 or 107.
m:ndk: The surrounding park is always accessible. Inside you usually go in for events or guided tours (Google listing hours 9am–8pm on weekdays and 10am–8pm at weekends, to be confirmed): you can't always walk in freely.
m:socialist: Open Tuesday to Sunday 10am–6pm, ticket office until 5:30pm, closed on Mondays and public holidays (National Gallery website). Ticket about €4 (8 leva = €4.09 on the website before the euro; reduced about €2, Thursdays about €1.50: euro amount to be confirmed). The park with the statues can be seen even when the inside is closed. It's about 5 km from the centre (south-eastern outskirts).
vd:banitsa: A small bakery specialising in banitsa, the filo pastry with white cheese, spinach or pumpkin that Bulgarians eat for breakfast, with ayran (a yoghurt drink) or boza.
vp:banitsa: A banitsa usually costs €2–4 with a drink (estimate, menu not seen). Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:izzy: A trendy café a short walk from the Banya Bashi mosque: eggs Benedict, avocado toast, cakes and carefully made coffee, in a courtyard full of graffiti.
vp:izzy: A brunch is around €8–14 («€€» on Google; menu not seen). Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:mabaker: A small café-bakery on Vitosha Boulevard: croissants, cakes and fresh sandwiches, with a few outdoor tables on a side street.
vp:mabaker: A coffee with a pastry is around €4–7 («€€»; menu not seen). Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:hlebar: A bakery with tables, on a quiet street in the centre: homemade bread, banitsa, meatballs and simple dishes of the day, in a cosy setting with an upstairs room.
vp:hlebar: A banitsa and a coffee are €4–8, a dish of the day €8–12 («€€», estimate; menu not seen). The bread runs out early. Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:gevrek: A small, much-loved bagel shop near the National Theatre and the park: hot bagels with lots of fillings, including egg and bacon, to eat in the nearby park. Little seating.
vp:gevrek: A bagel is around €3–6 (estimate, menu not seen). Closed on Mondays. Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:sunmoon: A vegetarian place a short walk from the pedestrian zone, with many vegan dishes too, homemade bread, banitsa and cakes. Home-style cooking and friendly service.
vp:sunmoon: Lunch for two with drinks is around €23 (recent review, «€€»; menu not seen). Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:sweetsalty: A café-bakery for breakfast and brunch on Vitosha Boulevard, with cakes, savoury pies and homemade juices; lots of vegetarian and vegan choices.
vp:sweetsalty: Breakfast is around €6–12 («€€»; menu not seen). Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:supastar: A place for soups of every kind, meat, vegetarian and vegan, with wholemeal bread baked on site: a hot, quick, light lunch, with tables upstairs.
vp:supastar: A soup costs about €4.50–6 (recent reviews; menu not seen). Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:filiika: A snack bar in an alley: a dozen hot toasties with different fillings, homemade lyutenitsa (pepper relish) and herb salt. The owner is very friendly and suggests what to try.
vp:filiika: A toastie is around €3–6 («€», estimate; menu not seen). Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:sonya: A vegetarian canteen in the Iztok district, handy after the Museum of Socialist Art: a different menu every day, with soups, salads and hot dishes.
vp:sonya: Lunch is around €6–10 («€€», estimate; menu not seen). Closed on Saturdays and Sundays. Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:moma: A Bulgarian restaurant on three floors with a garden, near Vitosha Boulevard: starters with lyutenitsa and cheeses, chilli beans, roast lamb and local wines (Rubin, Mavrud). Best to book for dinner.
vp:moma: Dinner with a starter and a main is around €18–28 per person («€€€»; menu not seen). Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:hadjcellars: A cellar tavern with stone walls, barrels and traditional furnishings: grilled meat, shopska salad, cold cuts and Bulgarian wines. In the evening there's often live music.
vp:hadjcellars: Dinner around €18–28 per person («€€€»; menu not seen). Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:izbata: A tavern with traditional furnishings serving classic Bulgarian dishes in generous portions: chicken kavarma, salads and fresh starters made daily, local beer and wine.
vp:izbata: A main course with bread and a starter is around €18–25 (recent review, «€€€»; menu not seen). Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:manastirska: A restaurant in an old house, with recipes inspired by Bulgarian monasteries: homemade bread, smoked sausages, mushrooms in butter, stews and the famous raspberry wine. A rustic atmosphere, a quiet setting.
vp:manastirska: Dinner around €18–28 per person («€€€»; menu not seen). Reviews are mixed on the service. Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:hadjhouses: The restaurant of the Hadjidraganov «houses», near the central station and the Zhenski Pazar market: traditional cooking with grills, pork knuckle and lamb, and live music in the evening. Best to book.
vp:hadjhouses: Dinner around €18–28 per person («€€€»; menu not seen). Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
vd:podlipite: A historic 1926 tavern, a listed cultural monument, in the Lozenets district: home-style Bulgarian cooking with vegetables and meat from its own farm, shopska salad, kachamak (polenta with cheese) and grills. Booking recommended.
vp:podlipite: Dinner around €15–25 per person («€€€», estimate; menu not seen). According to one review the kitchen closes at 9:30pm. Hours from the Google listing, to be confirmed.
cd:storiaboyana: The Thracian treasure and objects from antiquity, in the Boyana residence.
cx:storiaboyana: It's in Boyana, about 8 km from the centre.
cd:storiasofia: The city's history in the former bathhouse, next to the mosque.
cd:galleria: Bulgarian art from the 19th century to today, in the Royal Palace.
cd:vitoshacab: A gondola up the mountain on the city's doorstep, with walks in the nature park.
cx:vitoshacab: It's in Simeonovo, about 10 km from the centre.
cd:naturale: A collection of minerals, fossils and stuffed animals.
